title: DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives f on R^d, permitting nonconvexity, with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. A global lower bound a exists with f(x0)-a ≤ Δ. Parameters satisfy L>0 and Δ≥0; no minimizer attainment is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i evaluates g_i(x,ξ), with E[g_i(x,ξ)]=∇f(x) and E[‖g_i(x,ξ)-∇f(x)‖²]≤σ². Worker distributions may differ, but all estimate the same objective gradient. Samples are IID within each worker, and entire sample streams are independent across workers.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Timed distributed oracle with n computing workers and one server. Worker i requires h_i>0 time per completed gradient evaluation; pending computations can be aborted. Communication uses finite bit strings on directed server–worker links, with message duration l+b·s for s transmitted bits. Distinct links can operate concurrently; each directed link permits one pending message. Every algorithm message receives an additional 64-bit clock overhead.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean: Network; computation; communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean: clockBits; step.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform second-moment bound E[‖g_i(x,ξ)-∇f(x)‖²]≤σ² for every worker and query point, with σ≥0. No light-tail or almost-sure noise bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean geometry on R^d, where d is a public natural-number parameter.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Known heterogeneous computation times and a star network with latency l≥0 and time per bit b≥0. All Params are public, including d,n,h,l,b,L,Δ,σ,ε,x0 and the sample space; f, gradient maps and probability laws are supplied through the hidden instance and admissible oracle.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: Return a measurable point X∈R^d with integrable ‖∇f(X)‖² and E[‖∇f(X)‖²]≤ε, where ε>0.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Accuracy is in expectation over the product of algorithm and oracle randomness at the prescribed fixed elapsed-time deadline.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Execution must have finitely many events almost surely for every deadline up to the stated elapsed-time budget; output is taken from the algorithm's designated root.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The objective and stochastic-gradient assumptions are classical, while the setup additionally specifies heterogeneous computation times, concurrent star-network communication, finite-bit messages, latency, per-bit costs and finite-clock execution semantics.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Smooth Nonconvex Optimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥0 is an integer. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz for L>0, and a given point x0 satisfies f(x0)−flow≤Δ for a global lower bound flow and Δ≥0. A star network has n≥1 computing workers and a coordinator. Each worker returns unbiased stochastic gradients with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent samples across workers and calls. Computation and bit communication take time. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯ satisfying EP∥∇f(x¯)∥2≤ε, where P is the law of sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x), with the Euclidean norm ∥⋅∥. Worker i∈{1,…,n} has computation time hi>0. Communication has latency ℓ≥0 and time per bit b≥0. The algorithm receives d,n, a measurable sample space Ω, (hi)i=1n, ℓ,b,L,Δ,σ,ε, and x0∈Rd. The objective, stochastic-gradient maps, and sampling distributions are accessed through the oracles.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd. There exists flow∈R such that f(x)≥flowfor every x∈Rd,f(x0)−flow≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Stochastic gradients). For each worker i, there are a probability measure μi on Ω and a jointly measurable map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd. For every x∈Rd, the map gi(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable, its squared error is integrable, and EZ∼μi[gi(x,Z)]=∇f(x),EZ∼μi[∥gi(x,Z)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2.

Assumption 3 (Independent sampling). Let Q be the joint law of sample streams (ξi,k)i=1,…,n;k≥0 taking values in Ω. Each coordinate ξi,k is measurable. For each i, the sequence (ξi,k)k≥0 is independent and identically distributed with marginal law μi. The entire streams (ξi,k)k≥0 are independent across workers. Algorithm randomness is independent of these streams.

Assumption 4 (Computation and communication). The network consists of coordinator 0 and workers 1,…,n, with communication only between the coordinator and a worker. Queries may use any point of Rd. An accepted evaluation at worker i and point x takes time hi and returns (x,gi(x,ξi,k)), where k is the number of evaluations previously completed by that worker. Each worker can have at most one pending evaluation; further evaluation requests while it is busy are ignored. A pending evaluation may be aborted, in which case it produces no reply and consumes no sample. The coordinator performs no gradient evaluations.

Messages are finite bit strings. A payload of m≥0 bits sent along a directed coordinator–worker link takes time ℓ+b(m+64), including a fixed 64-bit overhead. The receiver obtains the sender’s identity and transmitted bits. Each directed link can carry at most one pending message; further submissions on that directed link are ignored until delivery. Distinct directed links can operate concurrently, including opposite directions of the same link. Computations at different workers and communication can also proceed concurrently.

The resource budget is an elapsed-time deadline T≥0. The algorithm must have only finitely many events up to every deadline t≤T, almost surely under P, the joint law specified above. Its output x¯∈Rd is taken from a designated node at time T. It must be measurable, ∥∇f(x¯)∥2 must be integrable under P, and the accuracy requirement is EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥2]≤ε.

import LongTails.TemplateDistributed
import LongTails.Setups.StarNetwork
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedSmoothNonconvex

open DistributedTemplate
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ+
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  h : Fin n → Time
  l : Time
  b : Time
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)

abbrev Samples (p : Params) := Fin p.n → ℕ → p.Ω
abbrev ComputeQuery (p : Params) := StarNetwork.ComputeQuery (Point p)
abbrev ComputeReply (p : Params) := StarNetwork.ComputeReply (Point p) (Point p)
abbrev CommReply (p : Params) := StarNetwork.CommReply p.n

noncomputable def system (p : Params) (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)) :
    Oracle (ComputeQuery p) (ComputeReply p) (CommReply p) (p.n + 1) :=
  StarNetwork.system ⟨p.h, p.l, p.b⟩
    (fun i x samples k => g i x (samples i k)) P

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n + 1
  Instance p := Point p → ℝ
  ComputeQuery := ComputeQuery
  ComputeReply := ComputeReply
  CommReply := CommReply
  Output p := Point p
  publicInput := id
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ 0 < p.L ∧
    0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ f x) ∧ f p.x0 - lower ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
      (μ : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)),
      O = system p g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (ξ : Samples p) => ξ i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, IID (fun k (ξ : Samples p) => ξ i k) (μ i : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
        IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (μ i) f (g i) p.σ
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
    ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedSmoothNonconvex
